visuals.title: Where it hurts
visuals.text: Deep, severe eye pain that can spread to the jaw or face, often with joint disease elsewhere.

visuals.title: Treatment steps
nodes: Severe: oral prednisolone or IV methylprednisolone

visuals.title: Why it hurts so much
nodes: Severe pain, worse on eye movement

glossary.Systemic lupus erythematosus: An autoimmune disease affecting skin, joints, kidneys, blood and other organs, with ANA antibodies.
glossary.RF-positive: Having rheumatoid factor antibodies in the blood, seen in rheumatoid arthritis.
glossary.Autoimmune disease: A disease in which the immune system attacks the body's own tissues.
glossary.Segmental: Affecting one section or sector rather than the whole eye.
glossary.Inflammatory markers: Blood tests such as CRP and ESR that rise with inflammation.
glossary.Ophthalmology: The medical specialty dealing with eye disease.
glossary.Ophthalmological emergency: An eye condition needing same-day specialist review to protect vision.
glossary.Topical: Applied directly to the surface, here as eye drops.
glossary.Ibuprofen: A common NSAID that reduces pain and inflammation.
glossary.Corticosteroids: Anti-inflammatory steroid drugs such as prednisolone.
glossary.Pulsed: Given as short courses of high doses, usually intravenously.
glossary.Immunosuppressants: Drugs that dampen the immune system, such as methotrexate.
glossary.Infiltrate: A collection of immune cells that has moved into a tissue.
glossary.Avascular: Having few or no blood vessels.
glossary.Vascular plexus: A network of interconnecting blood vessels.
glossary.Ischaemia: Inadequate blood supply to a tissue.
glossary.Scleral thinning: Loss of scleral thickness from inflammation; the sclera may look blue-grey.
glossary.Vasculitic: Caused by vasculitis, inflammation of blood vessel walls.
